references.label: Mediazona and BBC News Russian: named Russian military dead
references.text: A running count of Russian soldiers whose deaths are confirmed one by one from obituaries, regional notices, cemetery records and relatives' posts, updated roughly fortnightly. It is a floor, not an estimate of total deaths; the publishers say the true figure is far higher.

references.label: UALosses: named Ukrainian military dead
references.text: A volunteer database of Ukrainian service members confirmed killed, compiled from obituaries, memorial pages and official notices, with a public search. A floor rather than a total, and not an official figure.

references.label: President Zelenskyy's stated Ukrainian military deaths
references.text: In February 2026 the President put Ukrainian battlefield deaths at about 55,000, with a large number also listed as missing in action. Independent trackers consider the figure low; it is the government's own statement.

references.label: Russian Ministry of Defence claims
references.text: Russia's ministry publishes its own claims of Ukrainian losses in daily briefings. No machine-readable feed was found and the figures are not collected here; they reach the updates only through state-tagged agency reporting.

references.label: Kiel Institute Ukraine Support Tracker
references.text: The Kiel Institute's tracker records military, financial and humanitarian aid committed and delivered to Ukraine by donor government, released as a spreadsheet with each update. Read the release notes before comparing donors; commitments and deliveries differ.
